analysis.material_system: Calendered graphite-based negative electrode (anode). It is most likely flake-type graphite blended with a minor silicon-containing additive (SiOx or a Si-C composite). Observed: the dominant phase has low BSE signal, lamellar flake/lens shapes with internal cleavage cracks and frayed edges, and strong horizontal alignment, which is typical of calendered graphite. A minority (~5% area) of angular 2-7 um particles is clearly but only moderately brighter in BSE (well separated, not saturated, roughly 2.5x the graphite grey level in this rendering). That contrast is too weak for transition-metal oxides or Sn/Sb and fits Si/SiOx. Several of these particles carry 0.5-1 um rims. No high-Z cathode phase and no Cu current collector appear in the field. The exact chemistry of the bright phase (Si vs SiOx vs Si-C) needs EDS. Whether the electrode is pristine or cycled cannot be determined from these images.

phases.name: Graphite (active material)
phases.identification_evidence: Dominant low-Z phase in BSE. Flaky/lenticular particles carry internal cleavage cracks parallel to their long axis and jagged, peeled edges, and show strong in-plane alignment from calendering.
phases.appearance_by_detector: BSE: uniform dark grey with thin dark internal crack lines. Inlens: mid-grey with bright lamella/edge streaks; a subset (mostly in the upper ~9 um) appears near-black with smooth gradient bands from charging. ETD: mid-grey with faint striations and bright edges.
phases.morphology: Platelets/flakes and lens shapes, not spheroidized. Long axes ~10-30 um, thickness ~3-12 um, aspect ratio ~2-5. Imbricated stacking with long axes mostly within ~25 deg of horizontal.

phases.name: Si-containing additive, dense angular type (likely SiOx or Si-C)
phases.identification_evidence: Distinctly brighter than graphite in BSE (higher mean Z) but with moderate contrast. Angular shard-like habit and 2-7 um size are typical of milled SiO/Si-based anode additives. Particles sit dispersed in the graphite interstices.
phases.appearance_by_detector: BSE: bright, fairly uniform, sharp-edged; several have a ~0.5-1 um graphite-grey rim and a partial dark gap. Inlens: light grey with fine speckle, core-shell appearance, and fine horizontal striations on some. ETD: lighter grey than graphite, smooth.
phases.morphology: Angular polygons, shards and slivers (up to ~2 x 7 um), 2-7 um. Some have rims, gaps or internal cracks.

phases.name: Si-containing additive, granular/porous type
phases.identification_evidence: As BSE-bright as the dense type, but with a mottled internal texture and darker veins; Inlens shows a sponge-like nanoporous texture. Possible origins are a porous Si-C composite, agglomerated nano-Si, or fragmented/cycled SiOx; these cannot be distinguished here.
phases.appearance_by_detector: BSE: bright with a mottled, vein-like darker network. Inlens: fine granular/sponge texture with bright speckles. ETD: light grey, slightly rough.
phases.morphology: Rounded-irregular, agglomerate-like particles of 2-7 um. The largest is ~4.5 x 7 um at x~64-69 um, y~11-17 um.

phases.name: Carbon-binder domain (carbon black + binder, probably CMC/SBR)
phases.identification_evidence: Not separable in BSE because it has a similar low Z to graphite. Recognised in Inlens as fine-grained, nanoporous, bright-speckled material in interstices and as thin films on graphite edges.
phases.appearance_by_detector: BSE: dark grey, slightly mottled, merging with graphite. Inlens: lacy/spongy bright-speckled pockets, thin bright films, and some smooth light-grey flow-banded polymer-like domains. ETD: low-contrast textured grey.
phases.morphology: Patchy wedge-shaped pockets (1-5 um) at flake junctions plus sub-0.5 um films on particle surfaces; not a continuous network.

phases.name: Pores (open, not resin-filled)
phases.identification_evidence: Black in BSE. ETD and Inlens show pore walls and floors below the section plane, so the pores are open and unimpregnated.
phases.appearance_by_detector: BSE: black, with dark-grey floors in larger pores. Inlens: black with bright rims and visible sub-surface topography. ETD: dark with grey sub-surface walls.
phases.morphology: Mostly horizontal slits 0.1-2 um wide and 3-20 um long between flakes. A few irregular voids of 3-8 um at multi-flake junctions, plus thin intraparticle cracks.

porosity.character: Dominated by elongated slit pores parallel to the flakes (horizontal), ~0.1-2 um wide and up to ~20 um long. They form laterally connected in-plane channels. Through-thickness links are only narrow inclined gaps between tilted flakes, implying high through-plane tortuosity. Larger irregular voids of 3-8 um occur at multi-flake junctions (x~71-91 um, y~11-20 um; x~121-128 um, y~12-16 um). Fine cleavage cracks inside graphite add minor intraparticle porosity. No clear porosity gradient is visible across the 44.5 um height.
porosity.comment: The 9.8% pore class matches the visibly black area well, so it is a sound measure of resolved open voids. It is probably a lower bound, for three reasons. Floors and walls of open pores appear dark grey in BSE and fall into the solid class. Nanoporosity inside the carbon-binder domain is unresolved. Partial-volume pixels at narrow slits are classed as solid. My estimate of resolvable porosity is ~12-14%. Bulk electrode porosity is probably higher (calendered graphite anodes are typically ~25-30%), but that cannot be verified from a 2D section.

analysis.binder_carbon_network: Graphite and the carbon-binder domain (CBD) share the same BSE grey level, so the CBD is assessed only from Inlens. It appears in two forms. (i) Small wedge-shaped pockets (1-5 um) of fine-grained, nanoporous, bright-speckled material sit at flake junctions; they seem somewhat more frequent next to the bright Si-containing particles (low confidence). (ii) Thin lacy films (~0.1-0.5 um) line many graphite edges facing pores, though these are partly confounded with edge contrast. Coverage is patchy rather than a continuous network; large flake faces are mostly in direct graphite-graphite contact or bare. Inlens also shows smooth, light-grey, flow-banded domains of several um (e.g. x~72-79 um, y~24-27 um; x~91-96 um, y~30-36 um) that look like ordinary dark grey in BSE. These are most likely insulating polymer charging (binder-rich CMC/SBR agglomerates or partially infiltrated resin); inclined sub-surface pore walls cannot be excluded. Estimated CBD is ~3-5% of the section area (low confidence).
analysis.particle_packing_and_alignment: Packing is dense and calendered. Graphite flakes are stacked in an imbricated, shingle-like arrangement with long axes mostly within ~25 deg of horizontal; a minority are tilted 30-60 deg (e.g. diagonal flakes around x~60-75 um). Contacts are mainly long face-to-face boundaries separated by thin slit pores. The vertical image direction is very likely through-thickness (basal planes parallel to the current collector) and the 174 um horizontal axis is in-plane (high confidence). Si-containing particles are wedged into interstices between flakes, often with a partial gap, rather than embedded in graphite. Neither the current collector nor the coating surface is visible. This strip therefore comes from the coating interior at an unknown depth.

heterogeneity.description: Graphite morphology, alignment and the slit-pore network are fairly uniform along the width, with a local cluster of larger voids in the upper centre (x~71-91 um, y~11-20 um). The bright Si-containing phase is laterally uneven: ~2-3% area with mostly small particles in the left third (x<58 um), ~5% in the middle third, and ~8% with the largest particles in the right third (x>116 um). With only ~11-19 particles per third, part of this may be sampling noise, but the trend is visible. The non-uniform Inlens brightness (dark particles in the upper ~9 um) is an imaging artifact, not microstructure.

defects_and_damage.description: Many graphite flakes contain thin (<~0.1-0.3 um) dark lines and some lenticular voids parallel to the flake long axis, confirmed as real gaps by bright lines in Inlens. They are basal-plane delamination, either intrinsic to flake graphite or induced by calendering.
defects_and_damage.location: Throughout; clearest in large flakes, e.g. x~12-38 um, y~24-38 um, and in the centre (x~60-100 um)

defects_and_damage.type: debonding / core-shell gaps around Si-containing particles
defects_and_damage.description: Several bright particles are separated from the surrounding graphite, or from their own ~0.5-1 um grey rim, by a dark gap of ~0.1-0.5 um. Possible causes are volume-change debonding (if cycled), loss of coating adhesion, or milling relief; the images cannot decide between them.
Irregular voids 3-8 um across occur where flakes bridge rather than pack, in addition to the general slit porosity.
defects_and_damage.location: Upper centre x~71-91 um, y~11-20 um; right x~121-128 um, y~12-16 um; smaller ones scattered

defects_and_damage.description: Many flake boundaries show ragged, partly peeled lamellae that produce jagged pore walls. This is plausibly calendering damage, possibly accentuated by milling relief.
defects_and_damage.location: Throughout, most pronounced in the upper half

defects_and_damage.description: Some bright particles have a vein-like BSE texture and a sponge-like Inlens texture, and one dense particle shows an internal crack network. This could be an intentionally porous Si-C product or pulverisation of Si/SiOx during cycling; it cannot be determined here.
Bright-phase area fraction varies ~3x between the left and right thirds of the field (~2.5% vs ~8%).
defects_and_damage.location: Left third depleted; right third (x>116 um) enriched

imaging_artifacts.description: Many graphite particles, concentrated in the upper ~9 um and scattered elsewhere, appear near-black with smooth gradient bands in Inlens but look identical to other graphite in BSE and ETD. Polymer domains appear anomalously bright with flow-like banding. This is surface-potential contrast (possibly reflecting local electrical contact), not a second phase. It makes Inlens unsuitable for segmentation; BSE metrics are unaffected.
Inlens shows strong bright rims at every particle edge, crack and pore boundary (weaker in ETD), which merge with thin CBD films. BSE is largely unaffected.

The pores are not resin-filled. Floors and walls below the section plane are visible in ETD/Inlens and appear dark grey rather than black in BSE. Part of the true pore area is therefore classed as solid and pore boundaries are ambiguous.

ETD shows faint fine stripes on particle faces, and Inlens shows fine horizontal striations on some bright particles (e.g. x~131-138 um, y~24-30 um). These are consistent with ion-milling relief or scan noise.
Smooth, flow-banded light-grey domains in Inlens suggest softened or smeared polymer (binder or resin) from milling or beam heating.
A thin dark band appears along the lower-right edge (x~157-174 um, y~43.5-44.5 um), probably a pore or gap cut by the frame. It is too small to interpret and is not a current collector.

detector_insights.BSE: BSE is the most useful detector for quantification, with clean three-level contrast: pores black, carbonaceous material (graphite + CBD + binder) dark grey, Si-containing particles bright. It shows the cleavage cracks in graphite, the vein texture of the granular bright particles, and the rims and gaps around dense ones. Limitations: CBD, binder and graphite share one grey level; open-pore floors are dark grey; there is some shot noise at native resolution.
detector_insights.Inlens: Inlens gives the finest surface detail. It reveals the CBD as nanoporous, bright-speckled pockets and thin films, the sponge-like nanostructure of the granular bright particles, and the core-shell gaps around dense ones. It is, however, strongly affected by charging/voltage contrast (near-black graphite with gradient bands, bright flow-banded polymer) and by edge saturation, so it is suitable for qualitative use only.
detector_insights.ETD_or_SE: ETD gives topographic contrast with a small material component (bright particles are slightly lighter than graphite). It confirms that pores are open, since sub-surface walls are visible, and shows faint milling striations. It also shows that the Inlens-dark graphite particles are not a different material. It has less charging and edge saturation than Inlens and is useful for verifying particle boundaries.

analysis.threshold_metrics_assessment: Pore 9.8%: trustworthy as the fraction of clearly black open voids, but biased low as total porosity, by roughly 2-5 points. The causes are open-pore floors counted as solid, unresolved CBD nanoporosity, and partial-volume loss at narrow slits. Thin intraparticle cracks contribute a little real intraparticle porosity. Bright raw 6.4% and bright particle 5.2%: consistent with my visual estimate of ~5-5.5%, so trustworthy. The raw value includes small slivers and fragments, while the grey rims around bright particles are excluded. The count of 43 matches my visual count of ~45. The median equivalent diameter of 2.6 um is plausible but slightly biased low, by small fragments and by granular particles split along their darker internal veins; typical dense particles are ~3-5 um. The p90 of 5.4 um is credible. The middle class (~84%) lumps graphite, CBD, binder and pore floors and cannot quantify the CBD.
notable_features: Strong calendering-induced alignment of flake graphite parallel to the horizontal (in-plane) direction, giving shingle-like stacking and horizontal slit pores, which implies high through-thickness tortuosity
~5% area of moderately BSE-bright, angular 2-7 um particles, most plausibly SiOx or Si-C, in a dense and a granular/porous variant
Core-shell appearance with ~0.5-1 um rims and partial debonding gaps around several bright particles
Bright additive enriched in the right third and depleted in the left third of the field
Abundant intraparticle cleavage cracks and frayed edges in graphite
Pores are open (not resin-impregnated), so pore floors are visible in all detectors
Inlens voltage contrast darkens a subset of graphite particles, mostly in the upper ~9 um; this is an artifact, not a phase
No current collector or coating surface in the field: the strip is from the coating interior
analysis.summary: This apparently ion-milled, non-impregnated cross-section shows a densely calendered graphite anode. Flake/lens-shaped graphite particles ~10-30 um long make up ~77% of the section and are stacked with long axes horizontal, so the vertical direction is very likely through-thickness. About 5% of the area is a moderately BSE-bright, angular 2-7 um additive, most plausibly SiOx or a Si-C composite (EDS needed). It is unevenly distributed, enriched on the right, and several particles show rims and debonding gaps. Porosity is dominated by horizontal slit pores: the BSE threshold value of 9.8% matches the visibly black area but is likely a lower bound (~13% resolvable), while the bright-phase metrics (5.2-6.4%, 43 particles) agree well with the images. The carbon-binder domain is patchy and visible only in Inlens, which also suffers from strong charging and edge effects and should not be thresholded.
